summary.tpReason: Umbrella DNS telemetry records an allowed, successful A-record lookup of avsvmcloud.com from 17.81.146.1. CISA identifies this domain as SUNBURST/SolarWinds backdoor infrastructure and states the malicious DLL calls to victim-specific avsvmcloud.com domains. The indicator-specific event is therefore highly credible malicious beacon-related activity, although the root-domain-only lookup does not prove operator follow-on.
summary.fpReason: No endpoint or host identity is present (the DNS policy identity is literally HOSTNAME), and no process, SolarWinds binary, CNAME/subdomain, or secondary C2 was captured. CISA specifically cautions that traffic to avsvmcloud.com alone does not establish that the adversary leveraged the backdoor; a non-malicious test/scanner or incomplete context remains possible.
summary.whatHappened: At 2020-03-20 16:52:16.153Z, Umbrella logged 17.81.146.1 (InternalIp; DNS policy identity/Identities_0 both recorded as HOSTNAME) querying A record avsvmcloud.com. It was Allowed and returned NOERROR; the log associates ExternalIp 15.230.137.45. This is the sole avsvmcloud-related DNS record in available Umbrella telemetry from 2020-01-01 through 2021-01-31 and the sole query from that source/resolver pair in the ±7-day review. No corroborating firewall session, CrowdStrike host/detection, related Sentinel alert, AWS CloudTrail activity, Azure activity, Entra sign-in, or Windows event was found in the reviewed windows. No process/hostname attribution is available.
keyEvidence: Umbrella dnslogs: 2020-03-20 16:52:16.153Z — InternalIp 17.81.146.1 queried A avsvmcloud.com; Action Allowed; ResponseCode NOERROR; ExternalIp 15.230.137.45.

CISA AA20-352A says the malicious SolarWinds Orion DLL calls to victim-specific avsvmcloud[.]com domains and can receive secondary C2 instructions through DNS responses (https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa20-352a).

CISA AA20-352A also explicitly says traffic from an Orion device to avsvmcloud.com alone should not be treated as proof that the adversary leveraged the backdoor; secondary unexplained communications/CNAME resolutions require investigation (same source).
No avsvmcloud subdomains, CNAME-related entries, repeat beacons, or non-Allowed actions were present in the available Umbrella data (2020-01-01–2021-01-31).
researchDone: Reviewed the alert and raw solarigate_beacon_umbrella_CL event; validated action, A-record type, NOERROR response, identities, and both IPs.
Searched Umbrella from 2020-01-01 to 2021-01-31 for avsvmcloud and 2020-03-13–27 for 17.81.146.1/15.230.137.45; found exactly the one alerting lookup.
Searched CommonSecurityLog for associated DNS/HTTP/network sessions around the event; no records returned.
Searched CrowdStrikeHosts and CrowdStrikeDetections for either IP and relevant 14-day detections; no records returned, so no endpoint/process attribution or containment evidence exists.

Searched SecurityAlert, AWSCloudTrail, AzureActivity, Entra sign-ins, and SecurityEvent around 2020-03-20 for the IP/domain; no matching activity returned (AuditLogsHunting could not be time-filtered because its supplied schema lacks a time column).
Checked CISA AA20-352A for authoritative indicator context and interpretation limits of avsvmcloud traffic.
